column2: TPUSA's chief of staff and one of Charlie Kirk's closest friends of six years, standing feet away when the shot landed. What he did in the next thirty seconds — phone to ear, moving clear of the SUV — has been read two opposite ways ever since.
The TPUSA video executive who controlled audio and camera at UVU on September 10. He is also the executive named in the reported SD-card collection account, which TPUSA has answered.

Blake Neff has said he witnessed McCoy's calls, yet at 12:24:02 McCoy is reportedly alone in frame. The investigation file's own author calls it a timeline question and makes no accusation — and nearly every premise, from the word "witnessed" to the clock offsets, is soft.

A HADES-program aircraft reportedly made a 335-foot low pass near UVU at 12:24, thirty seconds after the shot. No aircraft can react in thirty seconds, so the pass is either coincidence or pre-positioning — and the file's own numbers conflict.

Everything citizen investigators flag inside the ten minutes from 12:18:30 to 12:28:30 on September 10 — five minutes either side of the shot. Second by second is where the strongest and the flimsiest claims sit next to each other.

A compiled timeline says the rifle was set down on the Losee roof at 12:24 — yet the Mauser was recovered in the woods. The tension resolves if the item was put down only to free both hands for the drop.

A compiled timeline says the roof figure limped all morning, then ran without a limp at 12:22. The entry carries no source and rests entirely on an observer's impression of gait in low-resolution video.

An unattributed passage back-extrapolates the rooftop runner's start to 12:23:28, two seconds before the shot. The arithmetic assumes constant velocity from a standing start, which is exactly where the two seconds come from.

Exploding-mic proponents read a 4K close-up as showing an object driven up under Kirk's shirt. The theory's own cited explosives expert says the mechanism would move the mic the other way — a claim rebutted by its own witness.
The investigation file records two shot times, 12:23 and 12:27, and asks itself which is right. The 12:27 figure is never sourced, and every other reconstruction in the file settles on 12:23:30.

Candace Owens released September 8, 2025 messages in which Charlie Kirk reportedly wrote that donor pressure was leaving him no choice. TPUSA reportedly confirmed the texts, which makes this one of the few items here with an organization's own confirmation behind it.

Flight trackers highlight an Egyptian-registered Falcon 7X parked at Provo the week of the assassination. It departed five hours before the shooting, which puts it hundreds of miles away — the detail the circulating posts leave out.
Anonymous accounts claim a man on Charlie Kirk's security detail once protected Benjamin Netanyahu, based on a side-by-side photograph. The posts do not even agree on who the man in the photo is.

Researchers claim a policy on Charlie Kirk was taken out right after he questioned October 7. The Wyoming filing offered as proof shows the LLC was formed five months before October 7 — the exhibit defeats the claim it was produced for.
The 2024 Hezbollah pager operation is invoked to argue a rigged-device killing is possible. It is a capability argument, not evidence: it establishes what can be done, never what was done here.

Charlie Kirk reportedly described an August 2025 Hamptons gathering as an intervention. Seth Dillon denied any angry confrontation, and Erika Kirk reportedly recalled a donor asking what would happen if he died.

An analyst reportedly claims raw GPS data put 44 foreign-registered phones near Charlie Kirk on September 10, sixteen of them Israeli. The dataset has never been published, so nobody outside the claim can test it.

Candace Owens reportedly attributes to Andrew Kolvet the words "it was supposed to be you," and says she and Tucker Carlson were on a list. No primary source for either exists in the investigation file.

Ten things citizen investigators flag about an alleged Israeli nexus — the donor texts, the foreign-registered phones, the life-insurance filing, the Hamptons meeting. Read it for the range: one item carries TPUSA's own confirmation, another is defeated by its own exhibit.

A former TPUSA representative alleges he was questioned about Israel at a bar during training, and told by two colleagues they were with Israeli intelligence. Single-source, no names, no documents — and recorded here as exactly that.

An analyst reportedly claims four of the alleged UVU devices later pinged at the Islamabad Serena during US–Iran talks in April 2026. The circulated graphic was admitted to be a recreation, not the data.

Eleven things citizen investigators flag about state and local agencies — the booking paperwork, the missing surrender footage, the paved-over courtyard, the GRAMA warnings. The list is ordered roughly by strength, and it thins out fast. Start at item one and watch the burden shift back onto the claim.

The claim is that no autopsy was performed. Utah seals medical examiner records during an active capital case, so "no public report" and "no report" are being treated as the same statement when they are not. A question with a published answer the questioner did not look for.

The sheriff who facilitated the surrender resigned, and so did UVU's president — offered as a pattern. No document links either departure to anything. Running the agency at the centre of the state's most scrutinized homicide ends careers by exhaustion too.

A contractor says on camera he was told "the governor and the FBI... want this done by Monday." Pavers went in four days after the shooting, over the ground that would carry any residue. The instruction is secondhand from an unnamed on-site coordinator.

The official account reportedly places the car at UVU at 8:29am and never says when it left. Add the unaccounted buildings beside the rifle drop and a screwdriver that appears in reporting but not in the charges. A probable-cause affidavit is a minimum-threshold document, not a case file.

Court material reportedly puts Tyler Robinson Mirandized at 6:25pm on September 11 — before the 8:04pm tip call, and ninety minutes before the Discord messages said to have caused it. Warning someone early is lawful and common. The surrender video would settle it in a minute.

Washington County reportedly told a records appeal there was no bodycam footage of the surrender, and the lobby CCTV had already purged at thirty days. Two independent systems, one empty moment. Both halves have mundane answers that required nobody to decide anything.

An anonymous direct message says Kirk's autopsy was signed by a young woman the medical examiner had never met. No name, no document, no second witness. It is recorded here only so it can be checked or retired rather than circulating forever.

Candace Owens argues there is no sworn written confession, and that a former deputy warned a frightened 22-year-old to come in before a raid. Prosecutors rarely obtain written confessions in capital cases, so the missing document proves less than it is asked to.

Four photographs of the transport SUV interior — a fragment on the seat rail, scattered debris, one blurred pane. Blurring is routine redaction applied by whoever prepares an image for release, and this set was not released by law enforcement.

A 112-page records production reportedly carries an internal message fourteen hours before the shooting: two men had turned up asking to talk to police about "a plan." Forty-four minutes later someone replied they were overstating their access. Nobody in the chat asked what the plan was.

Ten things citizen investigators flag about the hospital, the transport, the medical examiner and the autopsy. Several of these items are contradicted by the investigation file's own text, and these pages say so rather than tidying it away.

Two one-line entries ask why the body was flown out and why there is no burial site. The file rebuts itself: there was a public memorial at State Farm Stadium, and a grave's location is family privacy. Privacy is not concealment.

A broadcast screenshot shows a pale fragment whose edges look scorched, and one question: why is there burned material in the SUV? Nothing has been recovered, identified or lab-tested. What is being analyzed is a photograph of a photograph.

The earliest witnesses on camera all described a wound to the heart. The charging document describes blood from the left side of the neck. Eyewitness memory of sudden violence is famously wrong about wound location — which points the opposite way from coordination.

Two theories explain the snapped necklace, and they refute each other: one requires a fast projectile, the other requires no projectile at all. Presenting both as converging evidence is how a file talks itself into a conclusion.

Kirk was carried into an SUV roughly thirty-one seconds after the shot — no ambulance, no sirens. An anonymous caller adds that "a 911 call never came through" at the hospital. Hospitals do not receive 911 calls at all.

A reconstructed surgical timeline is said to end after the Jerusalem Post had already announced the death. Neither time is sourced, linked or archived — and a foreknowledge argument is a claim about two clocks, with neither clock shown.

A recirculated thread says Israeli IPs searched seven Timpanogos doctors weeks before the shooting. Google Trends reports normalized regional interest on a 0-to-100 scale and cannot report an IP address at all. Seven living physicians are named by a chart that cannot say this.

Kirk was taken to a Level IV hospital when a Level II trauma centre was reportedly closer. The investigation file gives two flatly incompatible sets of distances, neither sourced to any mapping record — and the conspiracy-friendly version is the unsourced one.

No exit wound, the neck is the exit, or there was no bullet at all: three theories argued from the same footage, which is itself evidence the footage does not decide it. No pathologist has endorsed any of them.

Social media posted before the shooting that reads, in hindsight, like anticipation — and the open question of whether anyone who wrote it was ever interviewed. Hindsight makes ordinary posts look prophetic, which is exactly why these are handled carefully.

Two posts dated September 9, 2025 from a student account, recirculated ten months later with one question attached: was the author ever interviewed? The account identity is redacted here, and no accusation is made against anyone.

Twelve things citizen investigators flag around Turning Point USA — the audit, the succession, the money, the SD cards. Most of the money items turn out to be lawful and disclosed on the very filings being cited as proof.

Candace Owens says a TPUSA cease-and-desist letter conceded a media drone flew for B-roll before the event while security drones were denied. She calls that a contradiction. Two different aircraft and two different approvals — a letter saying both is drawing a distinction.

One name, three incompatible roles: the man who silenced a witness, the witness who was silenced, and a bystander volunteer. The investigation file assigns all three to Cooper Brown in three separate passages. That is noise being mistaken for a signal.

George Webb says Tyler Bowyer was moved aside for refusing an outside audit, eight days before the assassination. A COO change is an ordinary personnel move, and Bowyer reportedly stayed publicly associated with Turning Point Action afterward — the opposite of what "fired" predicts.

Candace Owens cites unnamed Aspen Summit donors who say Charlie Kirk never made the recorded statement appointing his wife CEO. No donor is identified. A founder telling his board what should happen if he dies is ordinary succession planning.

A senior TPUSA executive who reportedly never works campus stops was at UVU on September 10 and took the camera SD cards. UVU was reportedly the opening night of a new national tour — exactly where a national events executive would be.

Web archives reportedly show Dan Flood listed as a TPUSA officer on September 1, 2025 and gone afterward with no announcement. A head of security whose principal was killed on his watch leaving quietly is the most predictable outcome imaginable.

A viral thread alleges $15.2M in insider-directed payments and missing 990s. No filing, page number or year is cited, and the headline figure rests on an arithmetic error. Related-party payments appear on a 990 because reporting them is the system working.

The investigation file records three times that a man in post-shooting imagery "looks a lot like" a sponsor representative. It alleges no conduct by him at all. A sponsor's executive attending the event his company sponsors is the deliverable, not an anomaly.

A former TPUSA representative says Charlie Kirk found a hidden $5M stock fund with zero employees. One ex-staffer, no document, no 990 line item — and nonprofits lawfully hold investment portfolios and fund employee retirement plans.

Candace Owens alleges TPUSA's new COO took a call right after the shooting with a man she believes is "Pierre Du Pont," with a billion-dollar partnership at stake. No call record, no confirmed identity, and the billion dollars has never been documented in any form.

The file says a "replacement" announced himself on Fox within hours — and then never names him, never links the segment, never quotes a word. Two unattributed list entries that disagree with each other are the whole of the sourcing.

The State noticed capital intent six days after the shooting, before the ballistics came back inconclusive. Read the ordinary explanation before the sinister one: in Utah an early death notice is what unlocks qualified capital counsel and funding for the defendant.

One post says 20,000 files, another says 600,000, and neither is sourced to a filing — a gap of more than an order of magnitude inside one investigation file. The timing objection survives the arithmetic; the numbers do not.

An inmate held in the same jail was moved around the preliminary hearing, and posters infer he is being positioned as a jailhouse informant. They concede it is the "only logical explanation" they could reach — not something any filing shows.

A thread claims Israeli IP addresses searched two Utah judges before the assassination. Google Trends publishes a normalized 0-to-100 interest index and does not expose IP addresses at all, so the tool cannot produce the output the claim describes.

A man was reportedly arrested inside the active crime scene in a lab coat with a long gun, released same-day on zero bail, and had charges quietly dropped. Commentators cannot even agree on what the rifle in the photo is.

Nine items about how the case is being adjudicated — closed hearings, a disclaimed extraction, a document dump, and an eyewitness the State never called. The section that limits every other claim, because a closed record cannot confirm or refute anything.

Prosecutors wrote that they did not intend to offer evidence from forensic extractions — and the entire public narrative of guilt is extraction-derived. Then an agent testified about a Cellebrite extraction in open court.

The one person who says he saw and filmed the roof figure in full black tactical gear was reportedly never called, and told police they had the wrong man. DNA testing on items along the escape route was reportedly stopped.

Lawyers described as Erika Kirk's opposed the defense's continuance while federal agencies had not produced files held since September. Utah gives a victim representative that right by statute — which is the answer, and also why the question keeps being asked.

A commentator back-calculates from a compressed clip that the runner started two seconds before the hit, and calls the withheld footage criminal. Every input in that arithmetic is an estimate read off video nobody has in full.

A FARA registration filed eight days after the killing, touching the same media network Kirk broadcast through — plus a reported TPUSA contact with a Hollywood synthetic-media firm. The file opens the section with "Can we confirm if this happened?"

Anti-drone equipment reportedly tested at Provo Airport during the exact week ending in Kirk's death, and DoD-badged contractors reportedly boarding an Egyptian Air Force jet there. The researcher states outright that he has corroborated none of it.

Sixteen drones claimed in the UVU footage, and an anonymous NCTC contact who reportedly said the same drone-capable group was behind Butler. Compressed phone video is also the single most reliable generator of false drone sightings.
A whistleblower self-reported being at Fort Huachuca the day before; no source places him in any meeting. The document obtained afterward confirms he was there — not who else was.

A broadcaster says that the day after naming names, Google image results for every person named went blank while unnamed people still returned results. He kept screenshots of the after, and nobody archived the before.

The one intelligence component built by statute to answer whether a foreign hand was present reportedly opened that inquiry and was told to stop. The question was not answered and found empty — it was reportedly not asked.

An Army-linked ISR jet reportedly made two abnormally low, slow passes near the venue. The investigation file gives the same two maneuvers three incompatible ways, which means at least two tellings are wrong and none shows its work.

A donor-linked Citation landed at Provo at 10:06 AM on September 10 and turned straight around — land, sit, leave. Candace Owens is asking ground crews who was aboard, which is a request for tips, not a finding.

The accusation is not that NSA did something — it is that the capability to identify the foreign phones alleged near Kirk sits forty minutes from the venue, and the answer has never been produced. The underlying dataset has never been published.

Eleven items about defense-intelligence proximity to the case: the flights, the installations, the surveillance capability, and the one federal foreign-nexus inquiry that was reportedly stopped. Ranked honestly, from the strongest item to the ones listed only so they can be retired.

The file's own words are "someone said," the company name is misspelled, and a second entry in the same list says the university owned the parcel instead. Published so it can be retired, not followed.

One sentence in a working list: the badge access list at the airfield ten minutes from campus was reportedly modified the day after. No document, no custodian, no before-and-after — an observation someone wrote down to check, and nobody checked.
A USAF C-37A reportedly sat at the Army's intelligence home and left the morning of September 9. No manifest or visitor log has been released.

An unnamed engineer reportedly walks a 3D model to a shot origin south of the roof narrative. The whole entry is four lines with no name, no method and no error bars — and the file asserts two other origins simultaneously.

A charred mass photographed in the SUV is argued to contain transmitter parts, down to a melted audio jack. The theory cannot settle which RØDE model it is matching, and no fragment has ever been tested.

A pastor's brother arranging backstage access is treated as sinister, and the innocent explanation is the one the file states and then discards. Published as a debunk, with the unsupported family speculation left where it belongs.

Uncompressed four-channel broadcast audio is argued to separate three events: a Mach cone, a muzzle blast around 120 metres, and a louder low-frequency peak roughly 46 metres away — right at the tent where Charlie was seated.
One numbered bullet, with the file's own author writing "Is that true" into the record as he wrote the claim down. No name, no footage, no date, and no description of what blocking would have meant.

A news helicopter is put over the Losee Center roof from about 1:38 pm, and citizen reviewers argue its footage shows no screwdriver where an officer reportedly found one. The argument turns entirely on timing and on what that camera could resolve.

The file asks in one line why the wireless mic sat under the shirt with a furry windscreen still attached. Under-shirt mounting is standard broadcast practice — and it is also the physical foundation the exploding-mic theory is built on.
Thirteen things citizen investigators flag about the venue, the setup, the equipment and the people physically on campus that day. The wider day, as distinct from the tight clock around the shot.

Maroon shirt and shorts at 8:29 am, black long-sleeve and jeans by 11:49, a pronounced limp at 11:50 that is gone by the 12:22 roof run. He is charged, not convicted, and the file itself lists these as questions.

The file carries this claim twice and never reconciles the two versions: an unnamed executive in a bare numbered item, and a named allegation by Candace Owens. TPUSA has reportedly said police instructed the removal.

Six campus officers, no ambulance staged, no outside law enforcement coordinated, and faculty never trained on active-shooter protocol — for a crowd the chief later put at 3,000. UVU has acknowledged more documents exist and reportedly refused to release them.

A light blue half-empty backpack leaves the car; a dark, nearly full one appears in the stairwell. Investigators put the usable interior at seventeen inches against a rifle the file itself measures at forty-three or more.

An unnamed acoustics engineer reportedly places the shot south, above the Teachers' balcony. This site's own Canon audio analysis puts the rifle near 120 metres on the Losee roof. Both cannot be right.

Everything citizen investigators flag as suspicious, sorted by who did it — state and local police, the FBI, an alleged Israeli nexus, US intelligence, and the defense. Sorting by actor rather than by topic is what makes the pattern visible.

Rifle-recovery photographs, tensions in the charged man's timeline, and repeated public appeals for attendee footage. An aggregator whose value is that it keeps asking the crowd for what the state has not released.

Transponder tracks, altitudes and timing for an Army ISR jet reportedly running low passes near Orem. Flight logs are not intent — but this is the primary-data layer under the strongest documented aircraft anomaly in the case.
Screenshotted threads that end up inside this site's Israel and Candace Owens photo clusters. A record of what circulated and when, kept because the screenshots outlive the posts.
Court-secrecy threads: the gag-order sequence and a civil-contempt fight most coverage skipped. Where the case goes quiet, this account keeps the docket visible.

Amplification of the claim that Israeli and Washington DC IP addresses searched for hospital and medical staff. The pattern claim is the whole argument, and it rests on Google Trends rather than server logs.
A broadcast anchor, not an investigator. His split-screen segment is the artifact that fixes who was presented to a national audience as an eyewitness, by whom, and when.

Published unsealed search-warrant texts attributed to the charged man and his housemate in April 2026. Primary documents rather than commentary — which is why the thread keeps being cited by both sides.

The Discord confession read against the clock: an 8:57 PM timestamp set beside the custody record. The account's position is that the messages were produced while the charged man was already held; no court has found that.
The claim that a drone-surveillance request for the event was made and reportedly denied by the campus police chief. If a document for it ever surfaces, the security-failure argument changes shape.
Hearing-room notes from July 2026 on the autopsy entered into evidence — gunshot wound of the neck, manner homicide — and how the pronouncement was framed. Court-record coverage rather than theory.
Threads on the reported shutdown of the NCTC foreign-assistance review and the scope fight around it. Every person involved is a living public figure, and nothing here is a finding.

The Salt Lake City CBS affiliate's own posts — the Medal of Freedom, the memorials, the National Day of Remembrance. Kept because the local-broadcast record is what national coverage later compressed.
Live narration of courtroom testimony that an officer's body-camera battery died on the roof. This thread is one of the few contemporaneous public records of that testimony.
The podcast clip where a former counterterrorism director talked about the strangeness of the case. That single interview is what turned a halted foreign-ties review into a public story.
Threads on the SUV interior photographs and the charred material inside them. Amplification rather than analysis — the value is seeing when each photo set entered circulation.
Bystander video argued to show a figure on a building before the shot. Whether the frame shows a person at all is exactly what is disputed, and the doubt stays attached to the claim.
A repost carried the claim that a September 10 assassination-target-list warning existed. The original is second-hand and unverified; it is recorded here so the chain of circulation stays visible.

FBI anomaly lists, witness video-deletion claims, donor texts, oversight questions and censorship flags from one prolific aggregator. Breadth is the point — and breadth is also why each item needs its own check.
Footage of a security-team member leaving immediately after the shot, plus critiques of how the medical response was handled. Presence and timing only; no wrongdoing is alleged against anyone named.

TPUSA financial filings, a surveillance-plane ownership thread, a domain chain, and a dual-mechanism reading of the cause of death. One of the few accounts working the paperwork rather than the frames.

Timestamp juxtapositions and rhetoric disputes that circulated widely in commentary about the case. Documented because the posts themselves became the argument; no allegation of wrongdoing is made here.
Frames the Hamptons donor meeting as an intervention and recirculates a day-after video. It is an interpretation of a meeting, offered as one, and the meeting itself is documented separately.
The ATF ballistics record worked hard: the fragment that reportedly could not be tied to a .30-06, and the sealed CBLA fight behind it. Document-anchored, which makes it unusual in this section.

The claim that three separate people confirmed Kirk's fear of Israeli retaliation, alongside Epstein-Mossad framing threads. Second-hand confirmation claims like this are the hardest thing on this site to test.
A latency challenge to the notification-order claims — who could have known what, and how fast. Useful precisely because it argues against a timeline many investigators had already accepted.
A second-hand allegation that the autopsy was signed off before it was finished, and a variant naming a different transmitter model. Both are recorded as unverified, and the page says so.
The defense-side reading: the state has association evidence and no causal bridge to the fatal wound. Whatever you make of the case, that is the gap the hearings have to close.
July 2026 hearing coverage, a rebuttal to the surrender-timeline version circulating online, and an ordinary explanation for the paving. The counter-argument voice this section needs.
Mossad-assassination theory posts and sustained FBI criticism, preserved in this site's Israel photo record. Kept as a record of what was claimed, not as a finding about any service.

Amplification of the claim that Israeli and Washington DC IP addresses searched for Timpanogos medical staff. The same search-pattern thread several accounts here carry, and it stands or falls with the underlying Trends data.
